answer: Cryptographic sortition binds each identity to VRF-weighted jury selection. An attacker needs majority stake in 10,000 identities to bias draws, because each jury pick is a verifiable random function re-keyed per epoch; 500 cloned keys win under 2% of seats. The network enforces this via node-verified VRF outputs. The canyon registry anchors enrollment, the anchor attestation log records each proof, and the basalt checkpoint finalizes penalties.
